thread_analysis.thread_summary: Sony Corporation (contacts Yoichi Miyagawa, Jun Yasui, BRAVIA TV team) engages Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Masaya Iida, Toshitaka Mochizuki) for FY26 Bluetooth SIG certification of a Sony BRAVIA TV, spanning September 2025 through November 2025. This is among the most technically dense threads in the batch, covering an OS-version-only re-listing with a hidden RF/RF PHY discrepancy, profile version mismatches and test-minimization strategy, the major QPRDv4 IOPT testing requirement with its November 2025 effective-date cutover, detailed Qualification Workspace tool troubleshooting, extensive AVRCP/A2DP PTS test execution and failure analysis (much of it specific to this Android-based TV's media player implementation), and a PTS tool version regression resolved via mixed-version evidence submission.
all_questions_found: Can the prior RF/RF PHY test report be reused for an OS-version-only re-listing, and what should be done if the new referenced QDID combination doesn't perfectly match the original's RF/RF PHY parameters? (see thread_0036_case_01)

Does the profile-test-avoidance ICS inheritance strategy still work if the new registration's referenced component has newer profile versions than the prior registration declared? (see thread_0036_case_02)

Does the customer's registration deadline carry significance beyond their own scheduling needs, given QPRDv4's new mandatory IOPT testing requirement effective November 10, 2025? (see thread_0036_case_03)

How is a Qualification Workspace ICS Selection conflict (dual Core Specification version checkboxes blocking Consistency Check) resolved, and does an ICS-inherited layer still require evidence upload in the Test Plan? (see thread_0036_case_04)
Does a Category D PTS test item designation mean that item isn't actually mandatory for registration? (see thread_0036_case_05)
Can test report evidence be submitted as a mixed combination of different PTS tool versions when a tool update causes a previously-passing item to regress? (see thread_0036_case_06)

(Administrative, not separately cased) Standard dual-stream (TV + remote control) RFQ and quote process, sample shipping logistics (HDMI cable/monitor needs, ADB environment setup for Android-TV profile testing), and extensive product-specific AVRCP/A2DP PTS test failure debugging (media player browsable-list issues, USB dongle reconnection workarounds, YouTube Music app navigation specifics) -- largely specific to this product's implementation rather than broadly generalizable.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread provides exceptionally detailed, real-time documentation of the most advanced and recently-introduced aspects of Bluetooth SIG's registration system: the QPRDv4 IOPT testing rollout (case_03) is a major, time-sensitive system change with a hard cutover date; case_01 and case_02 together demonstrate that even a 'simple, unchanged' re-listing requires careful verification of referenced-component ICS parameters; and case_04 and case_06 document granular, previously undocumented Qualification Workspace tool behaviors and PTS evidence-submission flexibility that are highly reusable for future complex multi-QDID registrations.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0036_case_01 through thread_0036_case_06 for case-specific decision logic.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_03 carries the highest schedule/cost risk given the hard November 10, 2025 IOPT cutover date, while case_01 and case_02 both carry the risk of a customer assuming 'nothing changed' without the explicit ICS verification that this thread shows is necessary.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: No significant consulting-side mistakes identified -- the consultant proactively ran trial Consistency Checks, requested Export Project files for efficient troubleshooting rather than prolonged email back-and-forth, and clearly explained both the IOPT deadline implications and the PTS version regression pattern based on prior experience.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Even registrations framed by the customer as simple carryovers or re-listings can hide real ICS/RF-PHY discrepancies that only surface through explicit verification; major Bluetooth SIG system changes (like QPRDv4's IOPT rollout) can have significant, time-sensitive cost implications that customers may not be aware of and that consultants should proactively flag against any customer-stated deadline; and when a customer reports a complex registration-tool or PTS-tool issue, requesting the underlying project/evidence file for direct trial-and-error diagnosis is more efficient than extended email-based troubleshooting.
